ordered_diagnoses: Myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and normal coronary arteries
salient_findings: Continuous chest pain for two hours
ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3 on initial ECG
Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography
key_facts: 37-year-old woman with no past medical history
Denies dyspnea, syncope, or prior similar episodes
No personal or family history of cardiovascular or thromboembolic disease
Vital signs: pulse 110/min, blood pressure 100/65 mmHg, respiratory rate 20/min, temperature 37 °C, oxygen saturation 95% on room air
Cardiac auscultation was normal
Neck veins were not distended
Initial ECG showed sinus rhythm with 2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 and V3
Second ECG showed a new right bundle branch block and resolution of the precordial ST-segment elevations
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated right ventricular dilatation and an estimated pulmonary arterial pressure of 60 mmHg

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and subsequent resolution, along with the absence of coronary artery stenosis and the presence of right ventricular dilatation, is consistent with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, also known as stress cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of evidence for coronary artery disease and the rapid resolution of ST-segment elevations make this less likely.

rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
rejected.why: The coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries, making dissection unlikely.

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic findings do not strongly suggest pulmonary embolism, and the echocardiography findings are more consistent with cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Acute pericarditis
rejected.why: The absence of pericardial friction rub and the presence of right ventricular dilatation and ST-segment elevation resolution make pericarditis less likely.
